It can be done. I'm gonna go ahead and suggest you not do so. If you absolutely feel an urge to upgrade (you won't get that much benefit as your wireless protocols are probably able to handle more throughput than your ISP even provides) then you can simply get an external wireless adapter with the appropriate rating, like 802.11 N or whatever the hell they're up to now. This will plug right into your USB slot and modern USB has ample throughput to more than adequate throughput to allow you to max out the bandwidth available.

Usually there's a little card that slides into a slot and then the antenna wires snap onto it. I wouldn't suggest going into your laptop without first finding disassembly instructions for your particular model. There are tons of them on youtube and you're likely to find something there. The problem is there's no standard way to take a laptop apart and the process varies a lot between models. I replaced the wifi adapter inside of one of my laptops some years back when the included one had issues with linux drivers but I don't think that particular issue comes up much these days.

Another option would be to disable the internal wireless adapter and get an external usb wireless adapter.
